originalTitle: Discogs’ Kevin Lewandowski can’t live without his AeroPress

content: Twenty-five years ago, Kevin Lewandowski founded Discogs, arguably the destination online for obsessive vinyl collectors and music nerds of all stripes. It is a marketplace for buying and selling records, obviously, but it’s also become so much more. It’s a shockingly comprehensive database that covers not just albums and singles, but all the various versions and pressings. It’s a really fun rabbit hole to disappear down when you’re trying to figure out what obscure pressing of Ministry’s The Mind is a Terrible Thing to Taste or Psalm 69 you had in high school, because you definitely blasted the cover of “Lay Lady Lay” all the time and 100 percent never owned Filth Pig. In the years since it debuted, Discogs has grown to be much more than just a site where audiophiles go to trade rare first pressings of Beach Boys records. There are forums, groups, user-created lists, and more. It’s part eBay, part Reddit, and IMDB — just specifically for music. With more and more people turning their back on the algorithm and rediscovering physical media, now seemed like a perfect time to check in with Lewandowski. What is your most indispensable tool? My AeroPress. I use it multiple times a day. In fact, I just made a coffee with it [sips coffee]. How many tabs do you have open right now? Probably around 30 on my work computer. My personal computer is worse — probably 40 or 50. Which social media platform do you use the most? I look at X and Instagram occasionally, but I don’t really post. What is your favorite gadget you’ve ever owned? It’s not really a gadget, but I like to tinker. Lately I’ve been playing around with Home Assistant software and built my own setup to control things like the garage door and outdoor lights. So I guess my favorite gadget is one I made myself. What is one thing you wish you had created? Probably a game like Rez, which came out around 2000. It’s a rhythm game where you’re almost controlling the music as you play, about as close to DJing as a video game can get. I’ve actually had an idea for my own version with a similar concept. It’s still just an idea, though. What do you do when you need to focus? I’ll either clear everything off my desk or change locations completely. Go to a coffee shop or sit outside. Sometimes I just need a different environment. What’s the last piece of physical media you bought? Records. I was at Mint Gallery in Portland last week and picked up four. I still really like going into a record store and finding something to bring home. And I also recently picked up three reissues from the Moodsville / Acoustic Sounds series. What would the tagline for your biopic be? The Secret Weapon. What’s the last GIF or meme you used? I don’t use memes very often, but one I was kind of proud of was putting a Discogs screen into a North Korean war room photo. I was advised that maybe it wasn’t one for the company chat.

chineseContent: 二十五年前，凯文·莱万多夫斯基 (Kevin Lewandowski) 创立了 Discogs，可以说是痴迷的黑胶收藏家和各种音乐迷的在线目的地。显然，它是一个买卖唱片的市场，但它也变得更加重要。这是一个令人震惊的全面数据库，不仅涵盖专辑和单曲，还涵盖所有不同的版本和唱片。当你试图弄清楚你在高中时读过的《Ministry》的《The Mind is a Terrible Thing to Taste》或《Psalm 69》中的晦涩难懂的压力时，这是一个非常有趣的兔子洞，可以消失，因为你肯定一直在抨击《Lay Lady Lay》的封面，并且百分百从未拥有过《Filth Pig》。自推出以来的这些年里，Discogs 已不仅仅是一个供发烧友交易 Beach Boys 唱片的稀有首张唱片的网站。有论坛、群组、用户创建的列表等等。它一半是 eBay，一半是 Reddit 和 IMDB——专门针对音乐。随着越来越多的人放弃算法并重新发现物理媒体，现在似乎是与莱万多夫斯基进行交流的最佳时机。你最不可或缺的工具是什么？我的爱乐压。我每天使用它多次。其实我只是用它泡了一杯咖啡[小口咖啡]。您现在打开了多少个标签？我的工作电脑上大概有 30 个左右。我的个人电脑更差——可能是 40 或 50。您最常使用哪个社交媒体平台？我偶尔会看看 X 和 Instagram，但我并不真正发帖。您拥有过的最喜欢的小工具是什么？它并不是一个真正的小工具，但我喜欢修补。最近，我一直在摆弄家庭助理软件，并构建了自己的设置来控制车库门和室外灯等东西。所以我想我最喜欢的小玩意是我自己制作的。什么是o
